name: WorldReach Cart Monitor
author: worldreach2026-Lewis

sections.description:
WorldReach Cart Monitor Free helps WooCommerce store owners understand what happens after shoppers add products to their carts. Monitor current cart sessions, see products and estimated cart values, identify carts with extended inactivity, and review recorded activity through checkout.

See what’s happening in your store:

  • Live Cart Radar: View current WooCommerce cart sessions with product names, quantities, thumbnails, estimated cart values, latest activity, and checkout status.
  • Cart activity overview: See quick statistics for active carts, current cart value, carts at checkout, and carts that appear abandoned.
  • Abandoned-cart detection: Identify carts with at least 60 minutes of recorded inactivity and no completed order. This is an indication only; it does not confirm that a shopper has abandoned a purchase.
  • Persistent Cart History: Review recorded cart activity, products, values, first and last activity, customer contact details when entered, approximate location when WooCommerce makes it available, and order outcome.
  • WordPress Dashboard widget: See cart counts, current cart value, and recent recorded cart activity without opening the Cart Monitor page. Hide the widget for your account and restore it later.
  • Discover Pro: Explore an informational preview of the separate Pro edition. Premium feature illustrations are clearly identified as sample data.

The Free edition focuses on cart monitoring and history. It does not send customer emails, create recovery coupons, or run automated recovery sequences. Those recovery tools are available in the separate Cart Monitor Pro product.

Want to explore the Pro experience? Visit the WorldReach Cart Monitor website to see the Pro product information and live preview.

WooCommerce must be installed and active.

Privacy

Cart Monitor stores WooCommerce cart session identifiers, product identifiers and names, quantities, estimated cart values, add-to-cart and checkout timestamps, order status, and billing name/email details when entered during checkout. It stores this information in custom tables in the site’s WordPress database.

The plugin includes WordPress personal-data exporter and eraser integrations for cart records associated with a supplied email address.

The plugin does not store raw visitor IP addresses or send them to a third-party geolocation service. When available, it stores only the approximate region/country returned by WooCommerce’s local geolocation lookup.

Site owners should disclose cart and checkout data collection in their privacy policy.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Upload the WorldReach Cart Monitor plugin through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, or install it from the WordPress Plugins screen after it becomes available in the directory.
  3. Activate WorldReach Cart Monitor.
  4. Open WooCommerce > Cart Monitor to view Live Cart Radar, abandoned-cart detection, Cart History, and Discover Pro.
  5. The WordPress Dashboard widget appears on the Dashboard. Use Hide widget in the widget footer to hide it for your account. To restore it, open WooCommerce > Cart Monitor and select Show Dashboard widget.
sections.faq:
Does Cart Monitor Free send abandoned-cart emails?

No. The Free edition provides cart monitoring, basic statistics, and Cart History. It does not email shoppers or automate cart recovery.

Does Cart Monitor require WooCommerce?

Yes. WooCommerce must be installed and active.

What does “appears abandoned” mean?

A cart is marked as appearing abandoned when Cart Monitor has recorded no cart or checkout activity for at least 60 minutes and no completed order is recorded. This is a detection signal only; the shopper may still return and complete the purchase.

Where can I view recorded carts?

Open WooCommerce > Cart Monitor. Live Cart Radar shows current cart sessions, Abandoned Carts lists carts that meet the inactivity rule, and Cart History provides a persistent record of carts Cart Monitor has seen.

Can I hide the WordPress Dashboard widget?

Yes. Use Hide widget in the widget footer. To restore it later, open WooCommerce > Cart Monitor and select Show Dashboard widget. You can also manage dashboard widgets using WordPress Screen Options.

Does Cart Monitor store visitor IP addresses or send them to a geolocation API?

No. The Free edition does not send visitor IP addresses to a third-party geolocation service and does not store raw IP addresses. It can store approximate region/country details returned by WooCommerce’s local geolocation lookup when available.

Where can I learn about Cart Monitor Pro?

Use the Discover Pro tab in the plugin, or visit https://worldreachcartmonitor.com/ to see the separate Pro product information and live preview.
sections.changelog:
1.0.6

  • Hardened dynamic SQL identifier handling with prepared identifier placeholders.
  • Added nonce protection to administrative tab navigation.
  • Replaced runtime table-alter SQL with dbDelta schema management.
  • Routed diagnostic errors through WooCommerce logging instead of PHP error_log().

1.0.5

  • Corrected database table creation and activation setup for clean installations.
  • Standardized plugin-specific identifiers and admin asset loading.
  • Fixed the Dashboard widget link to the Cart Monitor admin page.
  • Corrected translation text-domain usage and submission metadata.

1.0.4

  • Updated release metadata and documentation for the WordPress.org submission package.

1.0.3

  • Improved output escaping for product details displayed in cart tables.
  • Aligned the displayed Free edition version and WordPress/PHP compatibility headers with the 1.0.3 release.

1.0.2

  • Added a compact WordPress Dashboard widget with live cart counts, current cart value, and the five most recent recorded cart events.
  • Added a per-user Hide widget action and a restore control on the Cart Monitor page.
  • Added contextual links to Cart Monitor and the read-only Pro product tour.

1.0.1

  • Added a read-only Discover Pro product tour with clearly labelled sample data and a contextual link to Pro details.
  • No premium code, payment-gated controls, or remote demo assets are included in Free.

1.0.0

  • Initial standalone WordPress.org Free edition.
  • Added live cart monitoring with product thumbnails and basic cart statistics.
  • Added 60-minute abandoned-cart detection and persistent cart history.
  • Kept the initial Free package independent of licensing SDKs, automated recovery, customer email sending, and premium dashboard features.
  • Added WordPress personal-data export and erasure integrations and privacy-policy guidance.
